newsitem.title: UK: Oxford approves business school funded by tycoon.
newsitem.headline: Oxford approves business school funded by tycoon.

text.p: Oxford University on Tuesday voted to build a controversial business school funded by a Syrian-born tycoon who is a friend of former Conservative prime minister Margaret Thatcher.

Last November Oxford academics vetoed building the school on one of the university's cricket grounds but changed their minds on Tuesday when presented with plans to construct it elsewhere in the town.
The vote seemed to have ended a protracted row which started last year when tycoon Wafic Said offered 20 million pounds ($32 million) towards building the business school.
"The university has demonstrated its whole-hearted support for this important project," vice chancellor Dr Peter North said in a statement.
"We can now take full advantage of the enormous act of generosity by Mr Said and establish a business school worthy of standing alongside the very best schools in the world."
Said's donation is the single biggest gift to the university in 50 years.
